subject: Helios AI — dedicated capacity sizing & SKU tradeoffs (H100 / A100 / L4)

Subject: Dedicated capacity question — expected concurrency & SKU guidance

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've started sizing for a Q4 pilot and need some help narrowing hardware choices for a Dedicated contract. A few quick facts about our workload:
- Model family: mixed — a medium-sized Llama-variant for chat (approx 20B) and a smaller distilled model for embedding/semantic search.
- Typical context window: 4k tokens for the chat model, occasional 16k in night batch jobs.
- SLA: 95th pct generation latency < 800ms for median requests, burst concurrency up to ~220 qps during peak business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants a 12–24 month reserved proposal; they asked about H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs.

Can you outline recommended SKU mixes and the tradeoffs (memory vs throughput vs cost)? Also tell us any caveats around long-context batching and KV cache pressure.

If helpful, I attached a rough traffic export. Happy to hop on a call.

—Tom

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — expected concurrency & SKU guidance

Tom — great summary, thanks for the traffic dump. High level recommendation up front: a hybrid pool where memory-heavy chat instances run on H100s for headroom and long-context batch jobs use A100 nodes, with a scaled L4 pool for embedding/encoder workloads to minimize unit cost. Key bullets:

- H100 (memory-first):
  - Best for long-context (16k+) and models that require large KV cache (20B+ checkpoints).
  - Pros: better MLPerf-like throughput for mixed precision, larger VRAM headroom for concurrent KV caches; smoother latency when serving many long-context requests.
  - Cons: higher $/hr and less cost-effective for embeddings or small-model inference.

- A100 (balanced):
  - Good middle ground if you prefer more predictable cost; strong for batch/throughput-oriented tasks.
  - Pros: mature ecosystem, good quantization support, lower list price vs H100.
  - Cons: may need careful memory sharding for 16k contexts at high concurrency.

- L4 (cost-efficient/throughput):
  - Ideal for encoder-only models (embeddings, semantic search) and low-latency tiny chat models.
  - Pros: low cost per token, excellent for high qps embedding pipelines.
  - Cons: limited VRAM — not suitable for sustained 16k contexts or very large chat models.

Operational suggestions:
- Autoscale pools by route: route chat to H100 for pinned sessions (use affinity) and fall back to A100 when H100 capacity is saturated.
- KV cache strategy: enable prefix caching on the chat model and reserve ~20–30% of VRAM per active session on H100 to avoid OOMs at concurrency spikes.
- Batching: use continuous batching on A100 for nightly 16k batch jobs; keep L4 for streaming short requests to maximize cost efficiency.
- Hedging: propose a 60/30/10 split (H100/A100/L4) to start for your peak profile — we can tune after 30 days of telemetry.

I attached a short tradeoffs PDF and a capacity estimate spreadsheet based on your traffic (see helio_capacity_estimate_Q3.xlsx). If you want, Ben can run a quick microbenchmark using a snapshot of your sample workload.

Propose next steps:
1) Redwood runs bench tests on your sample traffic (we'll need API keys & sample prompts).
2) We produce a committed reserved quote + an ops playbook (tiling/eviction policies).
3) Pilot for 30 days, then finalize long-term commit.

Happy to jump on a call Monday if that helps.

Best,
Irene

Adding a couple of engineering nuances from the runtime POV:

- Memory accounting: if Helios' chat model has large attention key sizes, plan for ~1.2–1.4x VRAM overhead beyond model weights for per-request KV. On A100 that means tighter packing; H100 gives more breathing room.
- Tiling: for 16k jobs, consider sequence tiling and auto-eviction policies to keep peak memory bounded. We'll share our tiling knobs in the ops playbook.
- Quantization: running the chat model in 4-bit + QKV-friendly kernels on H100/A100 can reduce memory pressure ~30% but needs validation for hallucination/regressions.

Ben

Tom — thanks, forwarding procurement notes to pricing + legal. Quick answers inline and next deliverables below.

- SLAs: identical uptime SLAs across pools (99.9% baseline for Dedicated) — latency SLOs are route-level and documented in the ops playbook. H100-backed routes will have tighter latency SLOs in practice due to headroom; we'll call that out in the proposal. Burst capacity policies (reserved -> burst to shared) will be explicit in the quote.

- Minimums: pricing tiers start at a 50-slot reserved commitment across pools; lower commit is possible but affects discount bands. We'll include a stepped pricing table.

- Migration/runbook: attached "redwood_sku_tradeoffs_v1.pdf" includes a one-page migration summary plus the full ops playbook outline. The spreadsheet (helio_capacity_estimate_Q3.xlsx) has our preliminary slot math matching the 60/30/10 starter allocation.
